newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- AUG 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- AUG 11.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

-- The deputy finance minister Nick Christodoulakis stated that 'the percussions from the dollar's rise against the drachma are not beyond our control and do not unnerve the government'. He cited the opportunity for export-led growth for the entire European Union and a low participation of the dollar in Greece's external debt.

-- The second round of litigation over the use of the 'Eskimo' trademark will go ahead soon between Athens-listed Viometal-Eskimo SA on the one side and Elida SA along with the state Industrial Reconstruction Organisation (OAE) on the other.

-- In his opening speach at the Thessaloniki international traded fair in September the prime minister is expected to announce the provision of tax incentives for corporate expansion in the Balkans through venture capital funds.

-- The national economy ministry will take the first step towards the privatisation of state utilities and corporations through the public offering of convertible bonds in 1998, along the lines of France's successful privatisation policy.

-- The tourist industry will increasingly turn to the Athens capital market following the successful listing of passenger shipping and yachts companies in recent years. The next wave of listings from the tourist industry will come from large family-run hotel chains, helped by substantial incentives provided by development legislation.
-- Economic ministers and the Bank of Greece's management share the view that it is too early for the drachma to join the Exchange Rate Mechanism in the coming six months or so.

-- Subsidies to utilities and public corporations through the public investment programme of the 1998 Budget will grow by a maximum 4.0 percent, in line with the government's 1994-1999 Convergence Programme.

-- The recent revision of add-ons on interest rates in favour of loans taken in drachma over foreign currency loans are expected to lead corporations operating in Greece to set up foreign subsidiaries to circumvent the regulations and cut their debt servivcing cost.

-- Greek banks are preparing for the launch of new foreign currency deposit products following the recent lifting of remaining foreign exchange controls by the central bank. A potentially large source of income for credit institutions is commissions on conversion of funds between drachmas and other currencies. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
